In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNA backbone geometry in A-, B-, Z-, and mixed A-B-DNA structures has a high degree of variability.
the DNA backbone geometry in the A-DNA conformation is not uniform, and that the B-DNA conformation has a more rigid and uniform geometry than the A-DNA.
there is no such thing as a "standard" A-, B-, or Z-DNA confor-mation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sugar-phosphate helical DNA backbone is not a rigid rod, but is a flexible structure with the flexibility varying with the conformational class and with the sequence.
the backbone conformation of DNA in crystals is highly variable and depends on the sequence, the presence of modified bases, the solvent, and the crystal packing forces.
the DNA backbone geometry of the A-, C-, and Z-DNAs is very different from that of B-DNA, and the B-DNA backbone geometry is more variable in crystals than in solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the backbone geometry of the A-DNA crystal structures is not well-defined, with the sugar-phosphate torsion angle distributions overlapping with those for the B-DNA and Z-DNA crystal structures.
there is a significant degree of variability in the backbone geometry of DNA crystal structures.
there are no significant differences among the three DNA conformational types in the distributions of torsion angles.
